title: Sondow's conjecture on the Smarandache function
statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $S(n)$ be the smallest positive integer $j$ such that $n$ divides $j!$. **Sondow's conjecture.** The inequality

$$
n^2<S(n)!
$$

holds for almost all positive integers $n$. The paper proves the stronger assertion that, for every fixed real number $k>1$, $n^k<S(n)!$ holds for almost all positive integers $n$, so this conjecture is resolved.
source_name: Xiumei Li and Min Sha, “A proof of Sondow's conjecture on the Smarandache function”, arXiv:1907.00370 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00370

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Minimum coprime number conjecture for odd generalized Petersen graphs with k=3
statement:
Let $GP(n,3)$ be the generalized Petersen graph, with $n\geq 7$ odd, and let $\mathfrak{pr}(G)$ denote its minimum coprime number. **The $k=3$ minimum-coprime-number conjecture.** For every odd $n\geq 7$, 
$$
\mathfrak{pr}(GP(n,3))=2n+3.
$$
 The source states that this has been verified for small values of $n$, while a minimum coprime labeling in the general case is not known there.
source_name: John Asplund and N. Bradley Fox, “Minimum Coprime Labelings of Generalized Petersen and Prism Graphs”, arXiv:1908.06051 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06051

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2019). “Additional cases of $GP(n,1)$ were proven to be prime in . Dean proved the conjecture that all ladders are prime.”

title: Alternating-sum Catalan conjecture for reduced valid hook configurations
statement:
For $k\geq 1$, let $C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}{2k\choose k}$ be the $k$th Catalan number, and let $\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_n(312))$ be the reduced valid hook configurations with $k$ hooks on permutations avoiding $312$.

**Alternating-sum Catalan conjecture.** For every $k\geq 1$,

$$
\sum_{i=1}^k(-1)^{k-i}\left|\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_{2k+i}(312))\right|=C_k.
$$

The identity is one of the additional patterns suggested by the displayed coefficient triangle; the source gives no resolution status.
source_name: Maya Sankar, “Further Bijections to Pattern-Avoiding Valid Hook Configurations”, arXiv:1910.08895 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.08895

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

title: Kosyak et al.'s height conjecture for cyclotomic polynomials
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number. For a polynomial $f$, its **height** $h(f)$ is the maximum of the absolute values of its coefficients. **Kosyak et al.'s height conjecture.** For every natural number $m$, there is a cyclotomic polynomial having height $m$. The conjecture was put forward by Kosyak et al.; the source then proposes the analogous assertion for unitary cyclotomic polynomials.
source_name: Pieter Moree and László Tóth, “Unitary cyclotomic polynomials”, arXiv:1911.01743 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01743

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

title: Mizuno's modularity conjecture for normalized partition q-series
statement: Let $\alpha=(A_+,A_-,D)$ be a Cartan-like T-datum of finite type, let $S_\alpha$ be its associated finite abelian group, and let $\mathcal{Z}_{\alpha,\sigma}(q)$ be the partition $q$-series for $\sigma\in S_\alpha$. Write $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ with $\tau\in\mathbb{H}$, and let $c_\alpha$ be the rational number defined by the associated dilogarithm identity. **Mizuno's normalized partition-series modularity conjecture.** There exists a congruence subgroup $\Gamma\subseteq\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ such that, for every $\sigma\in S_\alpha$, $q^{-c_\alpha/24}\mathcal{Z}_{\alpha,\sigma}(q)$ is a modular function with respect to $\Gamma$. This is the precise modularity formulation for the partition $q$-series introduced in the paper; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
source_name: Yuma Mizuno, “Difference equations arising from cluster algebras”, arXiv:1912.05710 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05710

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

title: Central log-concavity conjecture for Gaussian binomial coefficients
statement:
For integers $n\geq 45$ and $13\leq k\leq n-13$, let

$$
\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]=\sum_r a_rq^r
$$

be the Gaussian binomial coefficient, so that $a_r=[q^r]\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. The sequence of coefficients is **log-concave at $r$** when $a_r^2\geq a_{r-1}a_{r+1}$. **Central log-concavity conjecture.** For any fixed $n\geq 45$ and $13\leq k\leq n-13$, the coefficient sequence is log-concave at every integer $r$ satisfying

$$
25<r<k(n-k)-25.
$$

Computations up to $n=430$ support this conjecture. It concerns the failure of global log-concavity for Gaussian binomial coefficients and predicts log-concavity throughout a broad central range, but no proof or disproof is given here.
source_name: Brendan Pawlowski, “The fraction of an S_n-orbit on a hyperplane”, arXiv:2002.08535 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08535

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

title: Square-placement Wilf-equivalence conjecture for three length-four patterns
statement:
For a distant pattern, write a square between two consecutive letters to indicate the constrained gap at that position. Consider the classical patterns $1234$, $1243$, and $2143$, and choose the same one of the three positions between consecutive letters in each pattern. **Square-placement Wilf-equivalence conjecture.** The resulting three distant patterns are Wilf-equivalent; for example,

$$
|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(1\square 234)|=|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(1\square 243)|=|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(2\square 143)|.
$$

The paper calls this conjecture surprising and notes that an analogous assertion for arbitrary Wilf-equivalent classical patterns is false, giving a counterexample in length four. It remains open in the stated special case.
source_name: Stoyan Dimitrov, “On permutation patterns with constrained gap sizes”, arXiv:2002.12322 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12322

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “Section mentions a few unresolved conjectures, namely Conjecture , and , all related to Stanley--Wilf type results.”

title: Degree formulas for the Euclidean joint signature of a generic plane curve
statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d$ denote the Euclidean joint signature for a generic plane curve of degree $d$. The multiprojective witness-set dimensions are $\boldsymbol{e}_1=(1,1,1,1,0,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{e}_2=(0,1,1,1,1,0)$. **Euclidean joint-signature degree conjecture.** For $d\ge 3$,

$$
\deg \overline{\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d}=12d(d^3-1),
$$

$$
\deg_{\boldsymbol{e}_1}\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d=8d^2(d^2-1),
$$

$$
\deg_{\boldsymbol{e}_2}\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d=4d(d-1)(3d^2+d-1).
$$

These formulas were suggested by monodromy computations, which were successfully run for curves of degree up to $10$; their validity for all $d\geq 3$ remains open.
source_name: Timothy Duff and Michael Ruddy, “Signatures of algebraic curves via numerical algebraic geometry”, arXiv:2005.04783 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04783

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

title: Nonvanishing determinant conjecture for the Atrahasis code construction
statement:
Let $n$, $k$, $d$, and $t$ be integers such that $n-1\geq d\geq k\geq 2$ and $d\leq t(d-k+1)$. Let

$$
\alpha=\binom{(t-1)(d-k+1)}{t-1}.
$$

The main theorem establishes that, when $\alpha\leq 3003$, there exists an $(n,k,d,\alpha)$-MSR code over some sufficiently large field. **Atrahasis-code conjecture.** The main theorem holds for all $\alpha$; equivalently, for every such choice of parameters, there exists an $(n,k,d,\alpha)$-MSR code over some sufficiently large field. The claimed extension is motivated by computations showing no counterexample for $\alpha\leq 3003$ and by the authors' belief that the determinant underlying both proofs is nonzero for all $\alpha$.
source_name: Iwan Duursma and Hsin-Po Wang, “Multilinear Algebra for Minimum Storage Regenerating Codes”, arXiv:2006.16998 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16998

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

title: Bipartiteness conjecture for graphs with the complete identity property after attaching trees
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. A graph has the **complete identity property** if every vertex can serve as the sink and the recurrent identity is the same configuration. If, for every vertex $v\in G$, attaching a single tree of size $1$ to $v$ results in a graph with the complete identity property, then

**Bipartiteness conjecture.** $G$ is bipartite.

The conjecture is motivated by a computer search showing that every connected graph with at most $10$ vertices having this property is bipartite, although not every bipartite graph has the property. Its general validity remains open.
source_name: Yibo Gao and Rupert Li, “Compatible Recurrent Identities of the Sandpile Group and Maximal Stable Configurations”, arXiv:2008.10079 (2020).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1109.4775](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.4775).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10079

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

title: Infinitely many prime values of the j-function coefficients
statement: Let $c_n$ denote the coefficients of the $j$-function considered in the paper. **Prime-value conjecture.** There are infinitely many $n$ such that $c_n$ is prime. The computation finds several prime values of $c_n$ up to $n=2\cdot 10^7$, but only the smallest listed value has been certified by ECPP; the conjecture remains open.
source_name: Fredrik Johansson, “Computing isolated coefficients of the j-function”, arXiv:2011.14671 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14671

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

title: Linear upper-bound conjecture for the largest singular value
statement:
Let $\sigma_{1,n}$ denote the largest singular value of the matrix associated with index $n$. **Largest-singular-value bound.**

$$
\sigma_{1,n} \leq \sqrt{2.0193n-0.7914}.
$$

This bound is suggested by the numerical homotopy experiment and is presented as a conjecture for the growth of the largest singular value.
source_name: Neil J. Calkin, Eunice Y. S. Chan, Robert M. Corless, David J. Jeffrey and Piers W. Lawrence, “A Fractal Eigenvector”, arXiv:2104.01116 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.01116

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

title: Auchiche–Hansen's proximity and distance eigenvalue conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 4$ vertices with diameter $D$, proximity $\pi$ and distance spectrum $\partial_1\geq \ldots \geq \partial_n$. **Auchiche–Hansen's conjecture.**

$$
\pi + \partial_{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor \frac{2D}{3} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor} > 0.
$$

This conjecture would strengthen a result of Merris on proximity and distance eigenvalues. It is refuted by a connected graph obtained from a path on 13 vertices by attaching sufficiently many pendant vertices; specifically, the construction gives a counterexample for all $n\geq 190$ pendant vertices.
source_name: Adam Zsolt Wagner, “Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks”, arXiv:2104.14516 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14516

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2021). “The conjecture regarding the location of the peak was disproved by Collins who showed that for paths the peak is at index approximately $\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)n$.”

title: Small-intensity lower bound for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation
statement:
Let $p_c(bb)$ denote the critical value for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane. **Small-intensity lower-bound conjecture.** There exists a $bb_0>0$ such that

$$
p_c(bb) > (\pi/3)\cdotbb
$$

for all $0<bb<bb_0$. The paper notes that the next-order expansion of $p_c(bb)$ could determine this inequality, although a different proof may also settle it.
source_name: Benjamin T. Hansen and Tobias Müller, “Poisson-Voronoi percolation in the hyperbolic plane with small intensities”, arXiv:2111.04299 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.04299

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

title: The maximum-average-degree conjecture for 2-distance coloring
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $Delta(G)=4$ and **maximum average degree** $\operatorname{mad}(G)<4$. The **maximum-average-degree conjecture.** asserts

$$
\chi^2(G)\leq 13.
$$

Here $chi^2(G)$ is the 2-distance chromatic number. The bound would improve the currently noted upper bound of $15$; the source gives no resolution.
source_name: Hoang La and Kenny Štorgel, “2-distance, injective, and exact square list-coloring of planar graphs with maximum degree 4”, arXiv:2205.07968 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.07968

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

title: Havet–van den Heuvel–McDiarmid–Reed planar square list-coloring conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. **Havet–van den Heuvel–McDiarmid–Reed conjecture.** 
$$
\chi_{\ell}^2(G)=\chi^2(G).
$$
 The conjecture was disproved in 2022 by Hasanvand, although it remains open for graphs with maximum degree at least $4$.
source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, “Coloring, List Coloring, and Painting Squares of Graphs (and other related problems)”, arXiv:2210.05915 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05915

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Fubini–Study Chern number conjecture for singular K3 surfaces
statement:
Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^3$ be a possibly singular K3 surface, and let $X_s$ be its smooth locus with curvature form $J$ induced by the Fubini–Study metric on $\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^3$. Suppose that the singularities of $X$ are isolated and of type $A_1$. **Fubini–Study Chern number conjecture.** Then

$$
\int_{X\backslash \operatorname{Sing}X} c_2(J)-c_1(J)^2=24=\chi(\operatorname{K3}).
$$

The conjecture is prompted by numerical Monte Carlo evaluations for the family studied in the paper, where the displayed identity appears for the singular examples. Its general validity for all possibly singular K3 surfaces satisfying the stated hypotheses is not established here.
source_name: Per Berglund, Giorgi Butbaia, Tristan Hübsch, Vishnu Jejjala, Damián Mayorga Peña, Challenger Mishra and Justin Tan, “Machine Learned Calabi-Yau Metrics and Curvature”, arXiv:2211.09801 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09801

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

title: McMullen's conjecture on 1-neighborly reorientations
statement:
Let $\nu(r,k)$ be the largest $n$ such that every uniform oriented matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements has a $k$-neighborly reorientation. **McMullen's conjecture.** For every $r\geq 3$, 
$$
\nu(r,1)=2r-1.
$$
 This conjecture has been verified for $r\leq 5$ but remains open otherwise.
source_name: Rangel Hernández-Ortiz, Kolja Knauer and Luis Pedro Montejano, “On k-neighborly reorientations of oriented matroids”, arXiv:2306.00414 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00414

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2023). “This conjecture has been verified for $r\leq 5$ , but remains open otherwise.”

title: Stein's minimum-semidegree conjecture for oriented paths
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $\delta^0(D)$ denote the minimum semidegree of an oriented graph $D$. **Stein's conjecture.** Every oriented graph with $\delta^0(D)>k/2$ contains every oriented path with $k$ edges. This would extend Jackson's result for directed paths to arbitrary orientations; it remains open.
source_name: Maya Stein, “Oriented trees and paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2310.18719 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18719

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

title: Uniqueness conjecture for a Stirling-number Diophantine equation
statement:
For integers $n$ and $m$, consider the Diophantine equation

$$
\binom{n}{4}+10\binom{n}{5}+15\binom{n}{6}=\binom{m}{2}.
$$

The displayed Stirling-number identity shows that this equation arises from equating $\genfrac\{\}{0pt}{}{n}{n-3}$ and $\genfrac\{\}{0pt}{}{m}{m-1}$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** The unique solution with $n\geq 6$ is

$$
(n,m)=(14,364).
$$

The authors found this as the unique solution in the computational range $6\leq n\leq 4.6\cdot 10^7$, while uniqueness for all $n\geq6$ remains open.
source_name: András Bazsó, István Mező, {Á}kos Pintér and Szabolcs Tengely, “Singmaster-type results for Stirling numbers and some related diophantine equations”, arXiv:2311.06080 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06080

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2023). “Unfortunately, the solution to the above conjecture is out of reach of current methods.”

title: Thomassé's conjecture for oriented graphs
statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph, and let $delta$ denote its minimum out-degree. **Thomassé's conjecture.** The graph $D$ contains a directed path of length $2\delta$.

This is the $g=3$ case of Thomassé's proposed strengthening of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture. The general conjecture is false for every $g\geq 4$, while this oriented-graph case remains open.
source_name: Yangyang Cheng and Peter Keevash, “On the length of directed paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2402.16776 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16776

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “The conjecture remains open for $g=3$, which in itself was highlighted as an unsolved problem in the textbook .”

title: The exact maximum for the four-by-four higher-dimensional queens board
statement:
Let $Q_{\max}(n,d)$ denote a maximum solution of the $(n,d)$-queens problem.

**Four-by-four board conjecture.** For every integer $d\geq4$,

$$
|Q_{\max}(4,d)|=2^d.
$$

This is presented as the special case $k=2$ of the preceding upper-bound discussion and is related to the cited work of Langlois-Ré millard, Müßig, and Róldan. The source provides no proof or resolution.
source_name: Tim Kunt, “The n-Queens Problem in Higher Dimensions”, arXiv:2406.06260 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

title: Square-root formula conjecture for maximum spread when $k=4$
statement:
For $k=4$, let $\operatorname{Msp}(n,4)$ denote the maximum spread among all realizable bases for the parameter $n$. **Square-root formula conjecture.** For every $n\geq6$,

$$
\operatorname{Msp}(n,4)=\left\lfloor\sqrt{n-2}\right\rfloor+2.
$$

This is an empirical formula proposed from tables of collected numerical data. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution.
source_name: Daniel Berend, Philip A. Ernst, Aryeh Kontorovich and Rishi Kumar, “Exact expressions for the maximal probability that all k-wise independent bits are 1”, arXiv:2407.18688 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18688

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

title: The normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial conjecture for almost classical flat knots
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an almost classical flat knot, and let $\bar J_\alpha(z)$ denote its normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial, defined using a minimal diagram of $\alpha$.

**Normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial conjecture.** For any almost classical flat knot $\alpha$, the normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial satisfies

$$
\bar J_\alpha(-1)=1.
$$

This was observed empirically for every almost classical flat knot up to $10$ crossings. Whether the identity holds for all almost classical flat knots remains open.
source_name: Jie Chen, “FlatKnotInfo: the first 1.24 million flat knots”, arXiv:2410.00216 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00216

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

title: The weak $d\times 2d$ equiangular tight frame conjecture
statement:
An **equiangular tight frame (ETF)** is a matrix with unit-norm columns, constant-modulus pairwise inner products, and frame operator proportional to the identity. The conjecture concerns complex matrices with $d$ rows and $2d$ columns.

**Weak $d\times 2d$ conjecture.** For every $d$, there exists a $d\times 2d$ ETF.

This conjecture was posed by Fallon and Iverson and is the weakest of the paper's hierarchy of existence claims. The source reports substantial partial progress, including verification of the broader all-dimensional claim through $d=165$ and numerical evidence through $d=1500$, but the universal statement remains open.
source_name: Joseph W. Iverson, John Jasper and Dustin G. Mixon, “More on the optimal arrangement of 2d lines in C^d”, arXiv:2410.17379 (2024).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2312.09975](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09975).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17379

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2024). “To date, Zauner's conjecture has been verified in scores of dimensions (see , for example), and numerical evidence supports the conjecture in hundreds of additional dimensions (see , for example).”

title: Strengthened lower bound for the sum of the two smallest graph eigenvalues
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\lambda_{n-1}$ and $\lambda_n$ denote its two smallest eigenvalues. **Strengthened eigenvalue conjecture.** One has

$$
\lambda_{n-1}+\lambda_n\geq -\frac{2n}{3}.
$$

This strengthens the original conjectured bound $c_3=\frac{1}{3}$ and was verified for all graphs of order at most $9$; the general case remains open.
source_name: Sida Li, “Strengthened upper bound on the third eigenvalue of graphs”, arXiv:2501.07494 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07494

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

title: Singh–Barman's hook bias conjecture for 2-regular partitions
statement:
Let $b_{t,i}(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $i$ in all $t$-regular partitions of $n$. **Singh–Barman's conjecture.** For every integer $k 3$, $b_{2,k}(n) b_{2,k+1}(n)$ for all $n 0$ and $ne k+1$.

This conjecture concerns the relative frequency of consecutive hook lengths in 2-regular partitions. It is false for odd $k$: the paper gives a counterexample at $k=3$, $n=82$, and proves that every odd $ke 3$ has infinitely many counterexamples. It is proved for $k=4$ and $k=6$, while the even cases beyond these remain open.
source_name: Wenxia Qu and Wenston J. T. Zang, “On the hook length biases of the 2- and 3-regular partitions”, arXiv:2501.13753 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13753

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2025). “This conjecture was proved by Craig, Dawsey and Han .”

title: Ustimenko's spectral bound conjecture for components of $D(k,q)$
statement:
Let $C\!D(k,q)$ be a connected component of $D(k,q)$, and let $\lambda_2$ denote its second largest eigenvalue. **Ustimenko's conjecture.** For all $k$ and $q$,

$$
\lambda_2\le 2\sqrt q.
$$

This is a universal spectral bound for the components; the source gives no resolution.
source_name: Felix Lazebnik and Ye Wang, “Some families of graphs, hypergraphs and digraphs defined by systems of equations”, arXiv:2503.07915 (2025).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2308.16728](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16728).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07915

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2025).

title: Narins–Pokrovskiy–Szabó conjecture on leaf-to-leaf path lengths in 1–3 trees
statement:
A **1–3 tree** is a tree in which every vertex has degree either $1$ or $3$. **Narins–Pokrovskiy–Szabó conjecture.** Every 1–3 tree $T$ of order $n$ has leaf-to-leaf paths of at least

$$
\log(n+2)-1
$$

distinct lengths. The source proves this claim as a consequence of a stronger theorem for arbitrary trees with bounded maximum degree, so the conjecture is solved.
source_name: Francesco Di Braccio, Kyriakos Katsamaktsis, Jie Ma, Alexandru Malekshahian and Ziyuan Zhao, “Leaf-to-leaf paths and cycles in degree-critical graphs”, arXiv:2504.11656 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11656

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2025). “Their conjecture, however, was disproven by Narins, Pokrovskiy, and Szab\'o who showed that there are arbitrarily large degree 3-critical graphs with no cycle of length 23.”

title: Grünbaum's equitable coloring conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, and let a **$k$-equitable coloring** be a proper coloring with $k$ color classes whose sizes differ by at most one. **Grünbaum's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with

$$
\Delta(G)<k
$$

has a $k$-equitable coloring. The conjecture was proved by Hajnal and Szemerédi in 1970.
source_name: H. A. Kierstead, Alexandr Kostochka and Zimu Xiang, “Results and Problems on Equitable Coloring of Graphs”, arXiv:2504.14711 (2025).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1901.08622](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.08622).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14711

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Viterbo's volume-capacity conjecture for convex domains
statement:
Let $c$ be a symplectic capacity and let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be a convex domain. Write $\operatorname{Vol}(X)$ for the Euclidean volume of $X$. **Viterbo's conjecture.** For every symplectic capacity $c$, 

$$
c^n(X)\leq n!\operatorname{Vol}(X).
$$

Haim-Kislev and Ostrover provided a counterexample using the Hofer–Zehnder capacity for the Lagrangian product of a regular pentagon and its $90^\circ$ rotation, so the conjecture is false in general. Its restriction to Lagrangian products $K\times_L K^{\circ}$ of centrally symmetric convex bodies remains an open question and is connected to Mahler's conjecture.
source_name: Alejandro Vicente, “The strong Viterbo conjecture and various flavours of duality in Lagrangian products”, arXiv:2505.07572 (2025).
references:
**9 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2405.16513](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16513), [arXiv:2405.18067](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18067), [arXiv:2311.02870](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02870), [arXiv:2303.12752](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12752), [arXiv:2206.07847](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07847), [arXiv:2106.07920](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.07920), [arXiv:1909.08967](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08967), [arXiv:1812.03039](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03039).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07572

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2025). “Recently, Haim-Kislev and Ostrover provided a counterexample to the Viterbo conjecture.”

title: Zhang–Kitaev equinumerosity conjecture for 213- and 321-avoiding permutations
statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_n^t$ be the set of permutations of length $n$ that become the identity after $t$ applications of the stack-sorting operation, and let $\mathfrak{S}_n^t(p)$ denote those that avoid the pattern $p$. **Zhang–Kitaev's conjecture.** For every $t\geq 1$,

$$
|\mathfrak{S}_n^t(321)|=|\mathfrak{S}_n^t(213)|.
$$

The paper constructs a bijection proving this equality, so the conjecture is solved.
source_name: Yang Li, Sergey Kitaev, Zhicong Lin and Jing Liu, “A bijection between 321- and 213-avoiding permutations preserving t-stack-sortability”, arXiv:2507.09187 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09187

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2025). “Knuth connected the stack-sorting algorithm with patterns in permutations by observing that $\S_n^1=\S_n(231)$.”

title: Zagier-duality modularity conjecture for type $D_k$ Cartan matrices
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}(D_k)$ be the Cartan matrix of the Dynkin diagram of type $D_k$, and let $f_{A,b,C}(q)$ denote the corresponding Nahm sum. **Zagier-duality conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, the Nahm sum

$$
f_{\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{C}(D_k),0,(1-k)/24}(q)
$$

is modular. This proposed identity is the dual counterpart of the modularity theorem proved in the paper for $f_{2\mathcal{C}(D_k)^{-1},0,-1/24}(q)$; its validity for all $k\geq 3$ remains open.
source_name: Liuquan Wang and Shangwen Wang, “Nahm sum identities for Cartan matrices of type D_k”, arXiv:2512.07790 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.07790

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2025). “The case $k=2$ of the Calinescu--Milas--Penn conjecture has been proved in .”

title: Modular transformation conjecture for the genus-two signature
statement:
Let $\sigma_2(q/p)$ denote the genus-two signature at a rational number $q/p$. For coprime odd integers $0<q<p$, consider the transformed fraction $q/(2q+p)$. **Modular transformation conjecture.** For any coprime odd integers $0<q<p$, one has

$$
\sigma_2\Bigl(\frac{q}{2q+p}\Bigr)-\sigma_2\Bigl(\frac{q}{p}\Bigr)=2q^2+2pq+p^2-1.
$$

This is an arithmetic analogue of the modular transformation law for the limiting function $\Lambda(\theta)$, suggested by the asymptotics of the genus-two signature along continued-fraction convergents. The identity was checked by computer for all $0<q<p<100$, but no proof or general resolution is given here.
source_name: Julien Marché and Gregor Masbaum, “Signatures in TQFT : Asymptotics and Modularity”, arXiv:2512.13450 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

title: The central binomial coefficient divisibility conjecture
statement: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $4$, and consider the central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$. **Divisibility conjecture.** The central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$ is divisible by $4$ or $9$ for every $n>4$ except $n=64$ and $n=256$. This is the paper's starting problem; the abstract describes the corresponding assertion for $n>256$ as open, and the paper does not provide a definite answer.
source_name: Sebastian Tim Holdum, Frederik Ravn Klausen and Peter Michael Reichstein Rasmussen, “Powers in prime bases and a problem on central binomial coefficients”, arXiv:2601.09510 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09510

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

title: Erdős's valuation growth conjecture for central binomial coefficients
statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. For an integer $a$, define $\epsilon_p(a)$ by

$$
p^{\epsilon_p(a)}\mid\mid a.
$$

**Erdős's valuation growth conjecture.** The $p$-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient satisfies

$$
\epsilon_p\left(\binom{2^{k+1}}{2^k}\right)=\frac{\log(2)}{2\log(p)}\,k+O(\sqrt{k}).
$$

This is motivated by a heuristic of uniformly distributed digits in the base-$p$ representations of powers of $2$ and by computer experiments for primes $p<200$. The source gives no proof or resolution.
source_name: Sebastian Tim Holdum, Frederik Ravn Klausen and Peter Michael Reichstein Rasmussen, “Powers in prime bases and a problem on central binomial coefficients”, arXiv:2601.09510 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09510

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

title: Merca–Ono–Tsai stabilization conjecture for partition numbers
statement:
For each fixed integer $d\geq 0$, define

$$
L(d):=\max\{n:p(n)\leq d+1\},
$$

and let $M_k(d)$ be the largest $n$ for which $p(n)$ is within $d$ of a $k$th power. **Merca–Ono–Tsai's stabilization conjecture.** There is a positive integer $N_d$ such that for all $k\geq N_d$,

$$
M_k(d)=L(d).
$$

The source attributes this to Merca–Ono–Tsai and gives no proof or resolution.
source_name: Summer Haag, Praneel Samanta, Swati, Holly Swisher, Stephanie Treneer and Robin Visser, “Repellent properties of perfect powers on partition functions: a heuristic approach”, arXiv:2601.18138 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18138

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “This conjecture has been verified for all $n \leq 10^8$ by Alekseyev , but still remains an open problem.”

title: Bal–DeBiasio conjecture on monochromatic tree covers
statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex $r$-edge-coloured graph, and let $tc(G)$ be the smallest number of not necessarily vertex-disjoint monochromatic trees whose vertices cover $V(G)$. **Bal–DeBiasio conjecture.** For every $r\geq2$, if

$$
\delta(G)\geq\frac{r(n-r+1)+1}{r+1},
$$

then $tc(G)\leq r$. The conjecture was settled affirmatively by Bucić, Korándi, and Sudakov, so it is solved.
source_name: Francesco Di Braccio and Viresh Patel, “Monochromatic cycle partitions of r-edge-coloured graphs with high minimum degree”, arXiv:2601.22117 (2026).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2403.12587](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12587), [arXiv:1708.01284](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01284).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22117

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2026).

title: Bivariate combinatorial interpretation of the q,p-Catalan triangle
statement:
Let $C_{n,k}(q,p)$ be the $q,p$-Catalan triangle, and let $\mathfrak{S}'_{n,k}(312)$ denote the set of $312$-avoiding permutations represented in the triangle. For a permutation $\pi$, write $\operatorname{inv}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{coinv}(\pi)$ for its inversion and coinversion statistics.

**Bivariate combinatorial interpretation.** For all $n\ge1$ and $0\le k\le n$:

$$
C_{n,k}(q,p)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}'_{n,k}(312)}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}p^{\operatorname{coinv}(\pi)}.
$$

The identity has been verified for $n\le5$; the source attributes a proof to W5. Its status should be checked against that reference.
source_name: Youssouf Wirdane, “Combinatorial study of the q-Catalan triangle and its generalizations”, arXiv:2605.14682 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

title: Kára and Král's exact minimum degree for 31-vertex cycle chords
statement:
For integers $n$ and $c$, let $f(n,c)$ be the least integer $d$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $d$ contains a cycle with at least $c$ chords. **Kára and Král's conjecture.**

$$
f(31,31)=8.
$$

Their known bounds are $8\leq f(31,31)\leq9$, so the conjecture asks whether the lower bound is sharp. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
source_name: Xiaozheng Chen and Bo Ning, “Cycle lengths and chords under chromatic and degree constraints”, arXiv:2607.15501 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15501

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2026). “Both conjectures were eventually proved by Gy\'arf\'as .”

title: The generating-function conjecture for $G(t,-k)$
statement:
Let $G(t,-k)$ denote the generating function considered in the paper, with $t$ a formal variable and $k$ an integer. **Generating-function conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 1$,

$$
G(t,-k)=\frac{2(k-1)!\,k!}{(2k)!}\left(\frac{\sin(t/2)}{t/2}\right)^{2k}\left[2^{2(k-2)+1}+\sum_{n=1}^{k-1}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{k-n-1}\binom{2k-1}{i}\right)\cos(nt)\right].
$$

The formula is based on explicit computations through $k\leq 60$ and is presented as a conjectural closed form for these generating functions; the source gives no resolution status.
source_name: Stefano Monni, Jun S. Song and Yun S. Song, “The Hurwitz Enumeration Problem of Branched Covers and Hodge Integrals”, arXiv:hep-th/0009129 (2000).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0009129

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2000).

title: Equality of parity edge-coloring numbers for bipartite graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph. Let $p(G)$ and $\widehat{p}(G)$ denote the minimum numbers of colors in a parity edge-coloring and a strong parity edge-coloring, respectively. **The bipartite equality conjecture.**

$$
p(G)=\widehat{p}(G).
$$

The paper gives examples with $\widehat{p}(G)>p(G)$, but all such examples contain odd cycles; whether equality holds for every bipartite graph remains open.
source_name: David P. Bunde, Kevin Milans, Douglas B. West and Hehui Wu, “Parity Edge-Coloring of Graphs”, arXiv:math/0602341 (2006).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602341

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2006).

title: 3D Euler regularity and singularity problem
statement:
For the incompressible Euler equations on boundary-free three-dimensional space, $\partial_t u+(u\cdot
abla)u=-
abla p$, $
abla\cdot u=0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,\infty)$, with smooth divergence-free initial data $u(0,x)=u_0(x)$ of finite kinetic energy $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|u_0(x)|^2\,dx<\infty$, determine whether the corresponding solution remains smooth for every $t\ge 0$. Equivalently, determine whether there exists such initial data and a finite time $T<\infty$ at which the solution develops a singularity and cannot be continued smoothly beyond $T$.
source_name: arXiv
references: - [A clarification on the distinction between nonlocal error and profile residual error in a computer-assisted proof of 3D Euler singularity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15174) — arXiv — Jiajie Chen, Thomas Y. Hou

title: Bridgeland stability (problem 1)
statement:
(Macri) Construct Bridgeland stability conditions on degenerate
 varieties, for example, the hypersurfaces with equations $x_0x_1\dots x_n=0$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$, especially for $n =2,3,4$. Given $[C]\in\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ arbitrary, is there a 
 description of the space of stability conditions on $C$? This is known some some irreducible nodal curves.

 (Schmidt) Are there Bogomolov type inequalities
 for stable objects on degenerate varieties?
source_name: AimPL: Stability and moduli spaces (posed by Macri, Schmidt)

title: Moment comparison
statement:
Consider the following problems:
	\begin{enumerate}
 \item Find the best $C>0$ such that for all $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to \mathbb{R}$, 
 

$$
\|f\|_2\le C^{\deg(f)}\|f\|_1.
$$

 \item For $1< p < q \le 2$, find the best $C_{p,q}>0$ such that
 

$$
\|f\|_q\le C_{p,q}^{\deg(f)}\|f\|_p.
$$

 \item How about the $d$-homogeneous analogs of the above two problems? Of particular interest, find the best $C>0$ such that for all $2$-homogeneous polynomial $f(x)=\sum_{i < j}a_{ij}x_i x_j$ over $\{-1,1\}^n$ for all $n\ge 1$, we have 
 

$$
\|f\|_2\le C\|f\|_1.
$$

	\end{enumerate}
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing

title: Finding Subsets of Vectors with Large Average Correlation (problem 1)
statement:
For $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and unit vectors $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n\in \ell_2$, consider the following two properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[(a)] $\langle v_i, v_j\rangle \le 2\varepsilon$ whenever $i\neq j$, and
 \item[(b)] for each $i$, there exists $A_i\subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ such that $|A_i|\ge n^{1-\delta}$ and
 $\langle v_i, v_j\rangle \ge \varepsilon$ for all $j\in A_i$.
\end{enumerate}
What is the largest $\delta$, in terms of $\varepsilon$, such that for any unit vectors
$v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n\in \ell_2$ satisfying (a) and (b), there exists $I\subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with

$$
|I|\ge n^{1-O(\delta)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{1}{|I|^2}\sum_{i,j\in I}\langle v_i, v_j\rangle = \Omega(\varepsilon)\, ?
$$
source_name: AimPL: Metric embeddings (posed by Alex Andoni)

title: ML vs.\ Bayes for spiked tensors
statement: Let $x_0$ be a uniformly random unit vector and observe $Y = \lambda x_0^{\otimes d} + W$ where $W$ is a symmetric tensor with $W_{i_1,\ldots,i_d} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ independently (up to symmetry). Let $\lambda^\mathrm{Bayes}$ and $\lambda^\mathrm{ML}$ denote the thresholds at which Bayes-optimal inference and maximum-likelihood estimation (respectively) achieve non-trivial correlation with the truth $x_0$. It is conjectured that $\lambda^\mathrm{Bayes} = \lambda^\mathrm{ML}$. These thresholds are also conjectured to be equal for the case $d = 2$ when $x_0$ has entries sampled i.i.d.\ from $\mathrm{Unif}\{\pm 1/\sqrt{n}\}$.
source_name: AimPL: Connecting communities via the block model (posed by Andrea Montanari)

title: Slicing problem in 3 dimensions
statement:
Suppose $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is convex, normalized to have volume $1$, and with its center of mass at the origin. Let 

$$
A_{ij} = \int_\Omega x_i x_j \, dx.
$$

The ball minimizes $\det A$. The problem is to find the shape that maximizes $\det A$. 

This functional is affine invariant under linear maps with determinant $1$ (volume preserving). The scale invariant form of the functional is $\det A/|\Omega|^{n+2}$, where here $n=3$.

In two dimensions, the maximizer is the triangle. In dimensions $n \geq 3$, the problem has been open since 1986: one possibility raised by Luis Rademacher is that it is reached by a simplex in dimension $n=3$.
source_name: AimPL: Symmetry-breaking of optimal shapes (posed by Luis Rademacher)

title: Generalizations (problem 2)
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A} = \{a_1, a_2, \dots\}$ be a sequence of integers with $(a_i, a_j) = 1$ for $i \not= j$. Let $\pi(n):= (-1)^{\#\{a_j:a_j|n\}}$. Is it true that 

$$
\sum_{n \leq X} \pi(n) = o(X)?
$$

Can we find a set $\mathcal{A}$ such that 

$$
\sum_{n \leq X} \pi(n+h_1) \dots \pi(n+h_k) = o(X)
$$

for all distinct $h_1, \dots, h_k$?

\begin{itemize}
 \item Remark: Let

$$
\lambda_y(p) = \begin{cases} 
 -1, &\text{if } p \leq y \\
 +1, &\text{if } p > y.
 \end{cases}
$$

If $y = X^{o(1)}$ then 

$$
\sum_{n\leq X} \lambda_y(n+h_1) \cdots \lambda_y(n+h_k) = o(X).
$$

For $k=2$ this was done by Daboussi-Sarkar.
\end{itemize}
source_name: AimPL: Sarnak's conjecture

title: Compute multi-point (spatial) distribution for KPZ with various initial data.
statement:
Compute multi-point (spatial) distribution for KPZ with various initial data. For example, with $\mathcal{Z}_0(x)=\delta_{x=0}$, let

$$
\mathcal{Z}(t,x)=e^{-\frac{x^2}{2t}+t^{1/3}A_t(t^{-2/3}x)-\frac{t}{24}}.
$$

What is the distribution $F(\xi_1, \xi_2)$ such that

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(A_t(x_1)\leq\xi_1, A_t(x_2)\leq\xi_2\right)=F(\xi_1,\xi_2)?
$$

Perhaps easier, show that as $t$ goes to infinity and space is scaled like $t^{2/3}x$, the process $A_{t}(t^{2/3}x)$ converges to the Airy$_2$ process in $x$.
source_name: AimPL: Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation and universality class
